tree.title: Marketing & Communications Policy
tree.summary: How Sublinear Financial advertises, communicates and pays for promotion: approvals, claims, pricing, disclosures, outbound messaging, social media, vendors and spend controls.

children.title: Scope, Definitions and Governance
children.summary: Who and what the policy covers, key terms, roles, exceptions, record keeping and training.

children.title: Purpose and scope
children.summary: This policy applies to every communication that Sublinear Financial, or anyone acting on its behalf, publishes to customers, prospects or the public, in any channel.
children.text:
This policy applies to every communication that Sublinear Financial, or anyone acting on its behalf, publishes to customers, prospects or the public, in any channel. It covers advertisements, websites, app screens, emails, text messages, social media posts, press material, sales scripts and sponsored content, whether created in-house or by an agency. A communication is in scope from the moment it is drafted for an external audience, not only once it is published. Where this policy and a product-specific procedure overlap, this policy sets the minimum standard.

The purpose of this section is to make sure that problems are caught before they reach a customer, not after. It does not replace professional judgement, but it sets the floor below which judgement may not go.

Procedure. The steps below are followed in order and none is skipped. First, the product marketing manager collects the information this section calls for and checks it against the current version of the landing page. Second, any point of doubt is raised with the Marketing Compliance Officer in writing, with the relevant extract attached. Third, the response is filed on the marketing compliance repository and the landing page is updated to reflect it. Finally, the product marketing manager diarises any follow-up date that this section or the response requires.

Guidance. Reasonableness is judged from the position of the Company, not the individual. Something that seemed sensible to a busy team at the time may still fall short of this section, and the record should show that the section was considered, not only that a decision was made.

Example: The content owner preparing an SMS for Sublinear FX finds that the supporting evidence is older than expected. They raise the question with the Compliance reviewer, who confirms that this section applies. The SMS is amended before it is released and the decision is recorded on the marketing compliance repository.

This section is most often applied together with section 1.4 (Policy ownership and annual review). Teams find it efficient to check the two at the same time and to make a single record covering both.

Records. Where this section is applied to a decision, the campaign lead notes the decision, the reasoning and the date on the campaign brief. A decision that is not recorded is treated as not having been made.

Example: The channel manager receives a request to treat a verbal assurance as sufficient. They decline, citing this section, and offer the compliant alternative instead. The request and the response are noted on the marketing compliance repository so that the same question does not have to be argued twice.

Interpretation. References to Legal include any deputy formally authorised to act in that capacity. References to writing include email and entries on the approval record, but not messages in chat tools unless they are copied to the record.

Section 1.2 (Definitions) deals with a related situation. The two sections are applied together, and a question that touches both is raised with the Marketing Compliance Officer once rather than twice.

Monitoring. The Compliance reviewer reviews a sample of items under this section monthly and looks in particular for items that were changed after they were confirmed. Repeated findings against the same team lead to additional training and, where necessary, a review of that team's permissions.

Responsibilities. Line managers make sure that everyone in their team who handles a paid social post knows this section and has completed the relevant training. Legal reports on compliance with this section to the Marketing Risk Forum at each risk forum.

Procedure for urgent cases. Urgency does not relax this section. Where time is short, the product marketing manager tells the Compliance reviewer at the outset what the deadline is and why it exists, submits whatever is complete, and makes clear what is still to follow. The Compliance reviewer may give a conditional view, but the conditions are recorded and the landing page is not released until they are met.

Example: An agency working on Sublinear Card proposes reusing material from another market. The Compliance reviewer reviews the proposal against this section and asks for the supporting evidence before any work proceeds. The agency's revised proposal is accepted and filed with the engagement record.

Frequently asked. Does this section apply when an agency rather than an employee produced the item? Yes. Does it apply if the item is only seen by a small audience? Yes. The only exemptions are those stated expressly in this policy or granted by a logged waiver.

Guidance. Where this section and a product or team procedure both apply, the stricter requirement is followed and the decision is noted on the approval record. A procedure can add to this section; it cannot subtract from it.

Edition note. This section is unchanged in substance from the previous edition. Minor drafting changes were made for consistency with the rest of chapter 1.

The requirement in this section exists because the cost of correcting a problem after the event is many times the cost of preventing it. It is read together with the rest of chapter 1, Scope, Definitions and Governance, and applies regardless of the channel, budget or urgency involved.

Guidance. When reading this section alongside an older paid social post, the current wording applies. Material that was acceptable under a previous edition is brought into line at its next review, or sooner if the Compliance reviewer so decides.

Records. The record is made at the time, not reconstructed later. Where a record has to be completed after the event, for example following an emergency, it says so and gives the reason.

This section is one of the controls on which the Company relies when it tells its regulators and its board that its external communications are controlled. For that reason it is applied in substance and not merely in form.

Procedure. (1) The campaign lead identifies whether this section applies to the landing page in question and records the conclusion on the approval record. (2) Supporting documents are attached to the record before the request is submitted, so that the reviewer sees the evidence and not only the assertion. (3) The Compliance reviewer checks the item against this section and either confirms the position or returns it with comments. (4) Comments are addressed in full and the item is resubmitted; partial resubmissions are not accepted. (5) The decision and its reference are recorded before the landing page is released or acted upon.

Guidance. Legal is the point of contact for questions about this section. Questions and the answers given are logged so that consistent positions are taken over time, and so that the next person to face the same question can find the answer.

Example: During a routine check, Compliance finds a sales script relating to Sublinear Invest that does not meet this section. The channel manager is asked to correct it, the earlier version is withdrawn so that it cannot be reused by mistake, and the record is annotated with what was found and how it was fixed.

Cross-reference. The record-keeping and escalation requirements that support this section are those of chapter 1; the related control in section 1.6 (Record retention) is applied in parallel.

Records. Internal Audit samples records under this section as part of its risk-based programme. Gaps found are reported to the Head of Compliance and tracked to closure.

children.title: Definitions
children.summary: The terms 'marketing communication', 'financial promotion', 'approver' and 'material change' have the meanings given in this section and are used in that sense throughout the policy.
children.text:
The terms 'marketing communication', 'financial promotion', 'approver' and 'material change' have the meanings given in this section and are used in that sense throughout the policy. A marketing communication is any message intended to promote the Company, a product or a service to an external audience. A financial promotion is a marketing communication that invites or induces a recipient to open, fund, use or retain a financial product. An approver is a member of Compliance authorised to sign off a financial promotion, and a material change is any alteration of the kind listed in section 2.5.

This section applies to every landing page and every comparable item, whoever produces it. Where it is unclear whether a particular case falls within it, the case is treated as in scope until The Marketing Compliance Officer confirms otherwise, and the question and answer are noted on the approval record.

Finally, the content owner diarises any follow-up date that this section or the response requires.

Guidance. Reasonableness is judged from the position of the Company, not the individual. Something that seemed sensible to a busy team at the time may still fall short of this section, and the record should show that the section was considered, not only that a decision was made.

The Marketing Compliance Officer reviews the proposal against this section and asks for written confirmation on each point this section covers before any work proceeds. children.title: The Marketing Compliance Officer
children.summary: The Marketing Compliance Officer approves every financial promotion before it is published and may withdraw any approval at any time.
children.text:

The Officer is appointed by the Head of Compliance, reports independently of the marketing function and may delegate day-to-day review to named deputies. Withdrawal of an approval takes effect when it is communicated to the content owner in writing. No commercial sponsor, campaign deadline or revenue target overrides the Officer's decision.

The content owner is expected to know this section well enough to apply it without looking it up, and to recognise the situations in which the Compliance reviewer should be consulted. The test applied throughout is a practical one: what the recipient will actually see and understand.

children.title: Exceptions and waivers
children.summary: Any departure from this policy requires a written waiver from the Marketing Compliance Officer, is limited to ninety days and is recorded in the waiver log.
children.text:

A waiver names the clause waived, the communication it applies to, the compensating controls and the expiry date. Waivers are never granted retrospectively and cannot be renewed more than once without the approval of the Head of Compliance. Verbal or email assurances that fall short of a logged waiver do not count as an exception.

children.summary: An approval expires twelve months after the date it is granted, and the communication must be re-approved before any further use.

A statement that is literally true can still mislead if the context, imagery or omission of a relevant fact would leave a reasonable reader with a false impression. Benefits are never given more prominence than the conditions and risks that qualify them. Where a communication is aimed at a less experienced audience, the standard is applied with that audience in mind.

children.summary: Words such as 'guaranteed', 'risk-free', 'can't lose' or 'certain' are prohibited for any product whose return, rate or value can vary.
children.text:
Words such as 'guaranteed', 'risk-free', 'can't lose' or 'certain' are prohibited for any product whose return, rate or value can vary. This covers Sublinear Invest, the variable rate on Sublinear Save and any currency transfer through Sublinear FX, where the rate moves until the transfer is executed. 'Guaranteed' may describe a contractual feature of a fixed-term product only when the guarantee is unconditional and the guarantor is named.

children.summary: Any quoted rate states whether it is fixed or variable, the date from which it applies and the conditions attached, and a variable rate is never presented as fixed.
children.text:
Any quoted rate states whether it is fixed or variable, the date from which it applies and the conditions attached, and a variable rate is never presented as fixed. For Sublinear Save the rate is always described as variable and the communication says that it can go down as well as up. Promotional rates that depend on a balance tier, a minimum deposit or a time limit state those conditions in the same view as the rate. The rate quoted is the rate in force on the planned live date, not a rate expected to be introduced.

children.text:

Rates are compared for the same product type, balance and term; fees are compared across the same usage pattern. The comparison is refreshed, or withdrawn, when the competitor's terms change. Competitor names are used factually, without logos or imagery that could suggest endorsement.

children.summary: A transactional message, such as a statement, security alert, payment confirmation or regulatory notice, carries no promotional content beyond a single footer line.

Transactional messages are sent regardless of marketing consent, which is why they are kept free of marketing. Whether a message is transactional is decided by its primary purpose, not by its template.

children.text:

children.text:

children.summary: Customer-generated content is reposted only with the author's written permission and after screening for claims that the Company could not itself make.
children.text:
Customer-generated content is reposted only with the author's written permission and after screening for claims that the Company could not itself make. Screening applies the same standards as a Company communication, including risk warnings where a benefit is described. Permission records the channels and period of use. Content from minors is never reposted.

The requirement in this section exists because experience shows that informal arrangements break down under deadline pressure. It is read together with the rest of chapter 7, Social Media, Influencers and Endorsements, and applies regardless of the channel, budget or urgency involved.

Procedure for urgent cases. Urgency does not relax this section. Where time is short, the campaign lead tells Compliance at the outset what the deadline is and why it exists, submits whatever is complete, and makes clear what is still to follow. Compliance may give a conditional view, but the conditions are recorded and the paid social post is not released until they are met.

Guidance. A common error is to apply the requirement to the headline but not to the detail. This section is not satisfied by a partial check; it is satisfied only when the item itself, as the recipient or counterparty will see it, meets the standard.

Example: An agency working on Sublinear Invest proposes a new creative route. The Compliance reviewer reviews the proposal against this section and asks for written confirmation on each point this section covers before any work proceeds. The agency's revised proposal is accepted and filed with the engagement record.

This section is most often applied together with section 7.9 (Live and unscripted content). Teams find it efficient to check the two at the same time and to make a single record covering both.

Records. Records under this section are kept in a form that a person unfamiliar with the sales script could follow: what was considered, what was decided, by whom and on what evidence. Abbreviations and internal shorthand are avoided.

Guidance. Where this section and a product or team procedure both apply, the stricter requirement is followed and the decision is noted on the approval record. A procedure can add to this section; it cannot subtract from it.

Example: A new joiner asks whether this section really applies to a sales script as small as the one they are working on for Sublinear Invest. Their manager explains that the section is about the nature of the item, not its size, and walks through the record that will be needed. The sales script goes through the normal process and the question is added to the team's induction notes.

Edition note. The wording of this section was shortened in the current edition. Arrangements made under the previous wording remain valid until their next scheduled review, after which this wording applies.

Guidance. When reading this section alongside an older email, the current wording applies. Material that was acceptable under a previous edition is brought into line at its next review, or sooner if the Marketing Compliance Officer so decides.

Responsibilities. The product marketing manager is accountable for compliance with this section in respect of the items they own. The Compliance reviewer provides second-line oversight and may escalate to the Marketing Risk Forum. Agencies and vendors acting for the Company carry the same responsibility under their contracts.

Frequently asked. Does this section apply when the counterparty is well known to the team? Yes. Does it apply if the item repeats something that was accepted last year? Yes. The only exemptions are those stated expressly in this policy or granted by a logged waiver.

See also section 6.13 (Links and tracking). Where both sections apply to the same press release, both are satisfied and the record notes each.

Procedure at hand-over. When responsibility for an app screen passes from one person to another, the outgoing owner records on the marketing compliance repository the status of each requirement of this section, what has been confirmed and what remains open. The incoming owner acknowledges the record. Nothing is assumed to have been done because it is usually done.

The purpose of this section is to make sure that problems are caught before they reach a customer, not after. It does not replace professional judgement, but it sets the floor below which judgement may not go.

Example: The content owner working on Sublinear Save is asked to proceed on the basis of an email rather than a record. Rather than proceed, they hold the press release and record the reason. Compliance confirms the position within the normal turnaround and the press release is released with the point addressed.

Interpretation. References to the Marketing Compliance Officer include any deputy formally authorised to act in that capacity. References to writing include email and entries on the marketing compliance repository, but not messages in chat tools unless they are copied to the record.

Monitoring. Results of monitoring under this section feed into the annual review of this policy, so that a requirement that is frequently misunderstood is clarified in the next edition rather than simply enforced more often.

Records. Where this section is applied to a decision, the product marketing manager notes the decision, the reasoning and the date on the review system. A decision that is not recorded is treated as not having been made.

This section is one of the controls on which the Company relies when it tells its regulators and its board that customers are told the whole story, not only the attractive part. For that reason it is applied in substance and not merely in form.

Procedure. The steps below are followed in order and none is skipped. First, the product marketing manager collects the information this section calls for and checks it against the current version of the landing page. Second, any point of doubt is raised with Compliance in writing, with the relevant extract attached. Third, the response is filed on the marketing compliance repository and the landing page is updated to reflect it. Finally, the product marketing manager diarises any follow-up date that this section or the response requires.

Guidance. The section is written for the ordinary case. An unusual case is not an exemption; it is a reason to involve Compliance earlier and to record the reasoning more fully than usual.

Example: During a routine check, the Compliance reviewer finds a sales script relating to Sublinear Invest that does not meet this section. The product marketing manager is asked to correct it, the earlier version is withdrawn so that it cannot be reused by mistake, and the record is annotated with what was found and how it was fixed.

Section 8.13 (Termination) deals with a related situation. The two sections are applied together, and a question that touches both is raised with the Marketing Compliance Officer once rather than twice.

Records. The record is made at the time, not reconstructed later. Where a record has to be completed after the event, for example following an emergency, it says so and gives the reason.

Guidance. Reasonableness is judged from the position of the Company, not the individual. Something that seemed sensible to a busy team at the time may still fall short of this section, and the record should show that the section was considered, not only that a decision was made.

Example: The content owner preparing a press release for Sublinear Card finds that the supporting evidence is older than expected. They raise the question with Compliance, who confirms that this section applies. The press release is amended before it is released and the decision is recorded on the review system.

Edition note. This section is unchanged in substance from the previous edition. Minor drafting changes were made for consistency with the rest of chapter 7.

Guidance. Legal is the point of contact for questions about this section. Questions and the answers given are logged so that consistent positions are taken over time, and so that the next person to face the same question can find the answer.

children.title: Live and unscripted content
children.summary: Only trained spokespeople go live on Company channels, and the applicable risk warning is spoken within the first sixty seconds.
children.text:
Only trained spokespeople go live on Company channels, and the applicable risk warning is spoken within the first sixty seconds. Live sessions follow an approved outline and a moderator is present to remove or respond to questions that seek personal advice. Recordings of live sessions are reviewed before they are made available on demand. A live session is ended if the risk warning cannot be given.

The channel manager is expected to know this section well enough to apply it without looking it up, and to recognise the situations in which Compliance should be consulted. The test applied throughout is a practical one: whether the Company would be comfortable explaining the decision to a regulator.

Procedure. The steps below are followed in order and none is skipped. First, the content owner collects the information this section calls for and checks it against the current version of the email. Second, any point of doubt is raised with Compliance in writing, with the relevant extract attached. Third, the response is filed on the review system and the email is updated to reflect it. Finally, the content owner diarises any follow-up date that this section or the response requires.

Guidance. A common error is to treat the requirement as a formality to be completed after the fact. This section is not satisfied by the fact that nothing went wrong; it is satisfied only when the record shows who decided what, and when.

The content owner is asked to correct it, the earlier version is withdrawn so that it cannot be reused by mistake, and the record is annotated with what was found and how it was fixed.

Section 7.2 (Employee personal accounts) deals with a related situation. The two sections are applied together, and a question that touches both is raised with Compliance once rather than twice.

Records. The record for this section comprises the dates on which the requirement was checked and by whom. Records are held on the campaign brief and retained in line with the retention requirements of this policy.

Interpretation. Words defined in chapter 1 have the same meaning here. 'Promptly' means as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within any period stated in this section; where none is stated, within the ordinary review turnaround.

Monitoring. Compliance with this section is monitored through complaint and query trends. Findings are rated low, medium or high and reported to the Marketing Risk Forum at each risk forum.

(4) Comments are addressed in full and the item is resubmitted; partial resubmissions are not accepted. (5) The decision and its reference are recorded before the press release is released or acted upon.

Responsibilities. Accountability for this section cannot be delegated by forwarding an email. A person who asks someone else to carry out a step remains responsible for confirming that it was done and for the record that shows it.

children.title: Giveaways and contests
children.summary: A giveaway or contest publishes its rules, eligibility and closing date, requires no purchase or account opening where the law so requires, and documents how winners are selected.
children.text:
A giveaway or contest publishes its rules, eligibility and closing date, requires no purchase or account opening where the law so requires, and documents how winners are selected. Prizes are described accurately and awarded within the stated time. Winners' names are published only with consent. Entry mechanics do not require participants to make claims about the Company's products.

This section applies to employees, contractors and agencies alike. Where it is unclear whether a particular case falls within it, the case is treated as in scope until The Compliance reviewer confirms otherwise, and the question and answer are noted on the campaign brief.

children.title: The advice boundary

children.title: Crisis and market events
children.summary: Scheduled promotional posts are paused during a declared incident or significant market event.
children.text:

Incidents include service outages, data incidents and public controversies involving the Company; market events are declared by the Chief Investment Officer or Compliance. Marketing checks the schedule queue within one hour of a declaration. Posts resume only when the incident lead confirms.

Subcontractors with access to customer data sign the same data-processing terms.

children.summary: The vendor indemnifies the Company for regulatory fines and remediation costs arising from non-compliant content the vendor created, and the vendor's liability is capped no lower than twelve months' fees under the contract.
children.text:

children.summary: Paid media is bought only through approved platforms using the corporate card or an approved purchase order, and personal cards are never used.

children.title: Goodwill credits to customers
children.summary: A frontline goodwill credit to a customer is capped at $50, and larger credits require manager approval and are recorded as goodwill.
children.text:
A frontline goodwill credit to a customer is capped at $50, and larger credits require manager approval and are recorded as goodwill. Goodwill credits are not used to settle complaints that should go through the complaints process. Credits above $500 require approval from the Head of Customer Operations. The goodwill ledger is reviewed monthly for patterns.

children.title: Sanctions and prohibited counterparties
children.summary: Every vendor and payee is screened against sanctions and prohibited-counterparty lists before the first payment and at least annually thereafter.
children.text:

Screening is performed by Finance using the Company's screening tool and the result is recorded against the payee. A potential match blocks payment until it is resolved by Compliance. Beneficial owners of agencies are included in screening.

children.summary: Splitting a payment, contract or purchase order into smaller amounts to stay under an approval threshold is prohibited.
children.text:
Splitting a payment, contract or purchase order into smaller amounts to stay under an approval threshold is prohibited. Related purchases from the same vendor for the same campaign are aggregated for approval purposes. Finance monitors for repeated payments just below thresholds. Splitting is treated as a serious breach regardless of whether each part was individually approved.
